verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents official SDKs in 15+ languages (TypeScript, .NET, Java) with React and Next.js integrations, and says it manages flags across web, mobile, and server-side apps, with both server-side and client-side SDKs referenced. The "consistent flag behavior" part is not documented: nothing shows identical evaluation semantics across SDKs, and a community evaluation notes Java SDK error reporting needs improvement. missing for 10: named mobile SDKs (iOS/Android/React Native), documentation of consistent evaluation semantics across SDKs, independent hands-on corroboration of cross-stack parity.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use official SDKs across my whole stack — backend, web, and mobile — with consistent flag behavior

citations.quote: SDKs & frameworks: Choose from 15+ popular languages like Typescript, .NET, Java, and more. Integrate with any framework, including React, Next.js, and more
Manage feature flags and remote config across web, mobile, and server-side apps.
**Server-side only**: enabling this prevents your flag from being accessed by client-side SDKs.
Run the Edge Proxy within in your own infrastructure and connect to it from your server-side SDKs
